findings.rationale: Under-recording of positives in Sex=1: at round 20 FL's observed/expected ratio for Sex=1 is about 0.51 (FNR 0.40) against about 0.95 for Sex=0, and the all-client Sex screen flags FL Sex=1 O/E at z=-4.8. Calibration is also off in the same direction (CITL +0.049, z=+3.1; prevalence 0.104 vs mean predicted 0.153), so observed positives fall short of what the features imply. Update norms are the largest in the federation (median norm ratio 2.78, z=+5.0) and the cosine to the median update turns negative from about round 14. Local AUC is normal (0.796), so this is a labelling bias rather than a poisoned update. Onset round is uncertain; the elevated update norm is already present in round 1, so 1 is used.

Same signature as FL: at round 20 SC's observed/expected ratio for Sex=1 is about 0.49 (FNR 0.42) while Sex=0 sits at about 1.19. The Sex screen flags SC Sex=1 O/E at z=-3.95. Overall CITL is +0.030 and prevalence (0.125) is below mean predicted risk (0.155). Update norms are high (median norm ratio 2.41, z=+4.9) and the cosine to the median update goes negative from about round 10. Local AUC is 0.797, which is normal.

Sex=1 under-recording again: at round 20 NJ's observed/expected ratio for Sex=1 is about 0.51, against about 0.94 for Sex=0. The Sex screen flags NJ Sex=1 O/E at z=-4.6. Prevalence (0.085) sits well below mean predicted risk (0.115), CITL +0.030. Update norms are high (median norm ratio 2.10, z=+4.3) and the cosine turns negative after about round 14. Local AUC is 0.819, which is normal. The evidence is somewhat weaker than for FL and SC because the NJ CITL flag is not raised.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the all-client views of update, performance, drift, feature and subgroup tools, then confirmed suspects with narrower queries. Three clients (FL, SC, NJ) show the same pattern: observed/expected for Sex=1 is about 0.5 against about 1.0 for Sex=0, with higher false-negative rates in that group, plus elevated and increasingly misaligned updates. This fits subgroup_bias (under-recorded positives) rather than poisoning, because their local AUC and data look normal. I reported them with moderate confidence; onset round is not pinned down by the noisy per-round drift data, so onset is set to 1. Not reported: GU (small n=237/708; citl z=-3.5, median norm z=3.6, Stroke and BMI feature anomalies, each near noise level), DC (drift z=3.9 and an AgeGroup cell with n=38), and VI (small client, drift in Income). Those leads are below the evidence bar. Budget is fully spent (20.0 used). Drift per-round results were too noisy to date onset precisely.
